Home.title: Preserving Knowledge,
Home.subtitle: Inspiring Research.
Home.description: The Majlis-e-Ilmi Foundation houses over 30,000 rare volumes and 48+ scholarly publications, serving researchers and academics across Pakistan since 1931.
Home.legacyDesc: Originally established in India, the foundation relocated to Pakistan in 1948. Today, we stand as one of the country's most respected centers of learning, housing rare manuscripts in Urdu, Arabic, Persian, and English.

Publications.headerDesc: Explore over 48 scholarly works published by the Majlis-e-Ilmi Foundation, recognized as authoritative references across Pakistan.

About.title: Our Heritage
About.subtitle: For over nine decades, the Majlis-e-Ilmi Foundation has stood as a beacon of scholarship, preserving the intellectual heritage of the region and fostering a deep culture of reading and research.
About.journeyDesc: Tracing our journey from 1931 to the present day.
About.t1Desc: Established in Jamia Islamia Surat, India, laying the groundwork for decades of scholarly research and publication.
About.t2Desc: Following the creation of Pakistan, the institution relocated, establishing its permanent home and continuing its mission of scholarship.
About.t3Desc: Housing over 30,000 rare volumes and supporting hundreds of M.Phil and Ph.D. scholars across Pakistan every year.
About.edP1: "Libraries are invaluable repositories of knowledge and wisdom, preserving the intellectual heritage, research, and collective experiences of generations. Books, in turn, serve as humanity’s most trusted guides, loyal companions, and powerful instruments of intellectual and moral development."
About.edP2: "The habit of reading not only enriches knowledge, awareness, and insight but also cultivates research aptitude, critical thinking, character formation, and intellectual growth. It is for this reason that nations maintaining a strong culture of reading and a deep connection with libraries are often at the forefront of academic, intellectual, and civilizational progress."
About.edP3: "In the contemporary era, there is a pressing need to further strengthen and expand this intellectual movement. By fostering a deeper engagement with knowledge and research among younger generations, we can contribute meaningfully to the development of a well-informed, enlightened, and intellectually resilient society."

Library.title: The Research Library
Library.subtitle: A sanctuary of knowledge. Home to over 30,000 rare volumes, manuscripts, and scholarly works in Urdu, Arabic, Persian, and English.
Library.c1Desc: Covering Qur'anic Studies, Hadith, Islamic Jurisprudence, History, Philosophy, Literature, and more.
Library.c2Desc: Over 700 university faculty and researchers have successfully completed M.Phil and Ph.D. projects using our resources.
Library.c3Desc: We welcome scholars, students, writers, and researchers from all backgrounds and schools of thought.
Library.guideDesc: To preserve our rare manuscripts for future generations, we ask all visitors to adhere to the following guidelines:
Library.g1: Valid CNIC or University ID is required for entry.
Library.g2: Bags, briefcases, and coats must be left at the reception desk.
Library.g3: Only pencils and paper are allowed in the reading rooms (no pens).
Library.g4: Books must be handled with care; rare manuscripts may require gloves.
Library.g5: Absolute silence must be maintained in the research areas.
Library.g6: Photography of rare manuscripts is strictly prohibited without prior permission.
Library.reqDesc: Looking for a specific title or researching a particular subject? Let our librarians know, and we will check our physical archives for you.
Library.reqBookPlace: e.g., Tafsir al-Kabir by Imam Razi
